title: Installing Tractor Brake System Components and Parts

lessons.title: Preparing and installing brake components
lessons.html:
Brakes are safety critical

A tractor with a loaded trailer on a hill or a public road depends on its brakes. A brake job done wrongly can kill the operator or other road users. Work exactly to the workshop manual, use correct parts and have your work checked.

Preparation

  1. Make the tractor safe: level ground, wheels chocked on the axle not being worked on, tractor on stands, key out.
  2. Confirm the brake type: dry drum or disc, or wet multi-disc in the rear axle housing, with mechanical, hydraulic or power actuation.
  3. Get the correct parts by serial number: friction discs, steel plates, seals, actuating pistons, master cylinder kits.
  4. Clean the area. For dry brakes, remove dust with a wet method and wear a suitable mask; never blow brake dust with compressed air.

Installing wet multi-disc brakes

  • Inspect the housing, brake shaft splines and actuating piston bore. Replace seals.
  • Soak new friction discs in the specified oil if the manual says so.
  • Stack friction discs and steel plates in the correct order and number. An extra or missing disc changes clearance and braking.
  • Lubricate piston seals with the specified oil and fit the piston carefully so seals do not roll or cut.
  • Measure brake pack clearance or piston travel if specified and adjust with shims.
  • Fit the housing or final drive with new seals and torque bolts in sequence.

Installing dry brakes

Fit new linings or discs as matched pairs on both sides so braking stays equal. Check drums and discs for scoring and wear limits. Clean friction surfaces with brake cleaner; never touch them with oily hands.

Hydraulic actuation parts

Fit master cylinders, lines and slave cylinders with new seals. Use only the brake fluid or oil type specified; many tractors use transmission oil, others use brake fluid, and mixing them destroys seals.

lessons.title: Bleeding, adjusting and testing brakes
lessons.html:
Bleeding the system

Air in a hydraulic brake system makes the pedal spongy and braking weak. Bleed as the manual describes, usually starting from the bleed point furthest from the master cylinder, keeping the reservoir topped up with the correct fluid. Continue until fluid without bubbles comes out and the pedal is firm. On power-brake systems that use tractor hydraulics, follow the specific bleed procedure with the engine running if the manual requires it.

Adjustment

  • Set pedal free travel to specification on each pedal.
  • Adjust so both pedals give the same travel and braking, so the tractor brakes straight when they are latched.
  • Adjust the parking brake so it holds on a slope with the lever in the specified notch.
  • Check that the brake light switch operates.
  • Check that front axle brake engagement (4WD engagement on braking) works if fitted.

Testing

  1. Static test: pedal firm, no sinking under steady pressure, no leaks at any joint.
  2. Parking brake test on a slope.
  3. Low-speed test in a safe area: each pedal separately brakes its wheel; latched pedals stop the tractor straight.
  4. Higher-speed test as the workshop allows, with pedals latched, checking for pulling, noise or judder.
  5. Trailer brakes: if fitted, test the trailer brake valve and coupling, and the breakaway function.
  6. Recheck fluid level and leaks after testing.

Bedding in

New friction material may need bedding in. Follow the manufacturer's advice and tell the operator to brake gently for the first period of use.

Sign-off

Brake work should be checked by the qualified mechanic or foreman before handover. Record parts, clearances, fluid type and test results on the job card. Explain to the operator: latch pedals for road travel and report any change in brake feel immediately.

Key points

  • Brakes are safety critical; follow the manual exactly and have the work checked.
  • Stack wet brake discs and plates in the correct order and number.
  • Use only the specified fluid or oil and never mix types.
  • Bleed until the pedal is firm and adjust both pedals equally.
  • Test static, parking, low speed and latched braking before sign-off.
